newsitem.title: GERMANY: German broker sees rising malting barley prices.
newsitem.headline: German broker sees rising malting barley prices.

text.p: Malting barley prices were on the increase after reaching lows under harvest pressure a month ago, German broker Jochen Mautner said in a client circular.
"Eastern European countries urgently need imports because in contrast to the European Union, they did not harvest a good malting barley crop," he said.
An early start to the winter in Canada would limit its export opportunities, making the EU the main supplier along with Australia.
Domestic EU supplies were ample from a 26 million tonne spring barley crop, up 38 percent from 1995, where some 25-30 percent qualified for malting purposes.
Mautner said the increase was due to area expansions, higher yields, adequate rain at the right time and slow maturing of the crop in July/August.

German farm price office ZMP quoted prices of malting barley at the Wuerzburg grain exchange at 325 marks, against 315-320 a month ago, but trade prices in Mannheim at 310-317.50 marks were unchanged from four weeks ago.
